artefacts.title: The label control killed seven variables at once
artefacts.null: 6.1% gain on data containing only survey structure and no physics
artefacts.control: Run the identical search on data that cannot contain the answer.

artefacts.title: A correlation whose sign belonged to the estimator
artefacts.null: the sign did not survive re-derivation
artefacts.control: Re-derive the estimator independently before quoting its sign.

artefacts.title: 38 sigma from data containing no effect
artefacts.null: the same significance on data constructed with no path effect at all
artefacts.control: Simulate the null separately for each algorithm and subtract it. A transverse decomposition orthogonal to distance cut the bias 60x for VoidFinder and 24x for REVOLVER, and still did not reach zero.

artefacts.title: Both axes contained the same term
artefacts.number: a confident correlation of plausible size
artefacts.null: the correlation is a restatement of the shared term
artefacts.control: Write down the construction expression for each axis and look for common factors, before quoting any correlation.

artefacts.title: Published fit noise with a preferred sign
artefacts.null: -0.0666 +- 0.0101 with the true effect set to zero
artefacts.control: Set the true effect to zero, redraw the catalogue inputs at their published uncertainties, and push them through the actual estimator.

artefacts.title: The same noise biased an amplitude low by a factor of 2.2
artefacts.null: -0.026 dex at error scale 0.25, -0.125 at 0.50, -0.336 at 1.00 -- monotonic in the input error
artefacts.control: Scale the input errors up and down and watch the estimator move. A real amplitude does not track the error scale of its inputs.

artefacts.title: A cosmic axis made entirely of shot noise
artefacts.null: 1.10 at 100,000 wells -- the amplitude is set by particle count
artefacts.control: Vary the sample size and watch the amplitude.

artefacts.title: A trend against r/R500 was a trend against r
artefacts.null: the normalisation carries no information the raw radius does not
artefacts.control: Check whether the normalising quantity is independent of the quantity being normalised.

artefacts.title: A permutation null too small to show its own width
artefacts.null: +1.64 sigma, p = 0.055, at 200 permutations on identical data
artefacts.control: Increase the permutation count until the null's standard deviation stops moving. Plot sd against draw count.

artefacts.title: Filtering out negative measurements manufactured a factor of two
artefacts.run: Runs BT and BU, retracted by Run BV, 2026-09-07
artefacts.number: pred/obs = 0.620, i.e. a factor 1.6 of missing gravity
artefacts.null: 0.914 +- 0.142 once the estimator is fixed -- consistent with 1
artefacts.control: Keep every point, weight by inverse variance, and work in linear space where the estimator is unbiased. Then check what the before-and-after difference was.

archive_traps.detector: Three detectors, ALL required, none sufficient alone. D1: the #Name: line must echo the EXACT identifier requested. D2: refuse any payload containing CatalogsExamined. D3: #Title: must match the expected author and year.

archive_traps.asked: observations near a sky position (ra, dec, radius parameters)
archive_traps.detector: Resolve targets by NAME, then reject any returned observation whose own RA/Dec lies more than a set tolerance from the target. The position is the detector, never the query parameter.

Two clusters of different dynamical state cannot share a thermal profile. When they appear to, the profile belongs to the instrument. The cause is energy-dependent vignetting: soft photons lose more effective area off-axis, so the band ratio hardens outward whatever the gas is doing.
Build the radial profile in fine bins, smooth it, then interpolate, rather than subtracting bin by bin.
